 Order

Heard Sri. Sharan N.Majage, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri. Yogesh D.Naik, learned AGA for the respondent No.1 and Sri. H.L.Pradeep Kumar, learned counsel for the respondent Nos. 2 and 3.
2.

Present petition is seeking to quash of the general award dated 10.04.2023 passed by the NC:
2023:KHC:37273 respondent No.3 as per Annexure-E in respect of land in Sy.No.12/2 measuring 05 guntas situated at Chapparadahalli Village, Kundana Hobli, Devanahalli Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District, and for a further direction to the respondents to consider the case of the petitioner as per Section 29(2) of the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Act (hereinafter referred to as 'Act' for short) to withdraw the general award amount deposited before the reference court.

3. Sri. Sharan N Majage, learned counsel for the petitioner reiterating the grounds urged in the memorandum of petition submits that the General Award has been passed in the case of the petitioner solely on the ground that a suit in O.S.No.6/2022 was pending consideration before the Civil Court and also the petitioner herein had not approached jurisdictional court claiming the Smt Gayithramma vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52961951/
2 compensation.

entities.text: Smt Gayithramma vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
He further submits that the acquisition of land belonging to the petitioner is not under challenge and petitioner is ready and willing to accept the compensation NC:
2023:KHC:37273 to be awarded under an agreement/ on the basis of consent.

4. Sri. H.L.Pradeep Kumar, learned counsel for the respondents-KIADB on the other hand submits that even as admitted by the petitioner at paragraph 3 of the petition that the Price Advisory Committee in its meeting held on 04.01.2023 has fixed compensation under the consent award/agreement at the rate of Rs.1,25,00,000/- per acre and that since there was a suit pending referred to above and also because petitioner did not approach jurisdictional court for claiming compensation, the general award was passed and awarded amount has been deposited before the reference court.

5. In response, learned counsel for the petitioner filed a memo dated 12.10.2023 stating that the suit in O.S.No. 06/2022 has been settled before Lok Adalath on 13.08.2022 and as on this date there is no dispute pertaining to the Schedule Property of the petitioner.
NC: 2023:KHC:37273 6.
Memo is taken on record.

7. Sri. H.L.Pradeep Kumar, learned counsel for the respondents-KIADB further submits that in view of the dismissal of the suit, if representation is made by the petitioner to the respondents 2 and 3,
the same will be considered in accordance with law.
8. Submission is taken on record.
9. In view of the above, present petition is allowed.

The general award dated 10.04.2023 passed by the respondent No.3 as per Annexure-E in respect of land in Sy.No.12/2, measuring 05 guntas situated at Chapparadahalli Village, Kundana Hobli, Devanahalli Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District is quashed and set aside.

The petitioner to file necessary application /representation within four (4)
weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order seeking compensation under Section 29(2) of KIAD Act.

The respondent Nos.2 and 3 is directed to consider the application /representation for award of NC: 2023:KHC:37273 compensation by way of consent award/
agreement under Section 29(2) of the KIADB Act and pass necessary orders within a period of three (3) months from the date of receipt of application/ representation of the petitioner.
The respondents-KIADB is at liberty to withdraw the amount that has been deposited before reference court pursuant to the general award passed by them.
Needless to state that in the event of any dispute, the general award would stand restored.
